title: Sound plays from the wrong device or the default output switches by itself
symptoms: Sound comes out of the monitor, TV or dock instead of my speakers or headphones
The default output changes after the PC wakes from sleep, the monitor turns off and on, or a device is plugged in
I set my speakers as default but Windows keeps picking another device after a restart
causes: An HDMI or DisplayPort monitor, TV or dock exposes its own audio device, and Windows makes it the default when it is connected or detected again
When displays sleep and wake, the monitor audio device disappears and reappears, so Windows falls back to another output
The preferred device was never set as the default (or default communication) device in the Sound control panel

signals: The current default render endpoint is an HDMI/DisplayPort or dock audio endpoint while an analog, USB or Bluetooth output is also active
The default render endpoint changed shortly after a display power event, resume from sleep, or a device arrival

fixes.title: Set your speakers or headphones as the default device
steps: Press Windows + R, type mmsys.cpl and press Enter.
On the Playback tab, right-click the device you want to use and select Set as Default Device.
Right-click the same device again and select Set as Default Communication Device if that option is available.
Select Apply, then OK.
On Windows 11 you can also go to Start > Settings > System > Sound and choose the device under Output; selecting it also makes it the default.

sources.signal: Official Microsoft troubleshooting page; Step 6 gives Set as Default Device (Win10) and Output selection sets default (Win11)
Microsoft Q&A, top 'Most helpful' answer (3 helpful votes) gives mmsys.cpl > Set as Default Device; not marked accepted

Dell KB 000125484: Windows may change the default playback device when a DP/HDMI cable is connected or on resume from sleep; set the wanted device as default. Content read from search excerpt; direct fetch failed

fixes.title: Disable the monitor or TV audio device you do not use
steps: Press Windows + R, type mmsys.cpl and press Enter.
On the Playback tab, right-click the monitor, TV or display audio device you do not use (often named after the monitor, or NVIDIA/AMD/Intel High Definition Audio) and select Disable.
Select OK.
To undo, right-click an empty area of the Playback tab, select Show Disabled Devices, right-click the device and select Enable.
Do not disable a device that you use for sound, such as TV speakers you listen through.

title: Audio device is disabled or hidden and does not appear in the sound list
symptoms: My speakers or headphones are missing from the output list in Sound settings
I clicked Don't allow or Disable on a sound device and now I have no sound
The output drop-down is empty or cannot be changed
causes: The audio endpoint was disabled in the Sound control panel or set to Don't allow in Settings
The audio device was disabled in Device Manager
The Sound control panel hides disabled devices by default, so they look missing

signals: An audio endpoint exists in the disabled state (DEVICE_STATE_DISABLED)
A device in the MEDIA class reports Device Manager problem code 22 (disabled)

fixes.title: Allow the device again in Sound settings
steps: Open Start > Settings > System > Sound.
Select the device (under Output, or under All sound devices on Windows 11) to open its properties.
On Windows 11, select Allow so the device is enabled. On Windows 10, make sure the Disable check box is cleared.

sources.signal: Official Microsoft troubleshooting page, Step 5: check devices have not been disabled by mistake
Microsoft staff answer (Mosken_L - MSFT), 100+ helpful votes, for a device set to Don't Allow on Windows 11

fixes.title: Show disabled devices in the Sound control panel and enable the device
steps: Press Windows + R, type mmsys.cpl and press Enter.
On the Playback tab (or the Recording tab for a microphone), right-click an empty area and select Show Disabled Devices.
Right-click the greyed-out device and select Enable.
If it should be your main device, right-click it again and select Set as Default Device.
Select OK.

sources.signal: Microsoft staff answer (Mosken_L - MSFT), 100+ helpful votes; exact mmsys.cpl Show Disabled Devices > Enable steps
Official Microsoft troubleshooting page, Step 5 (enable device) and Step 6 (Set as Default Device in Sound control panel)

fixes.title: Enable the audio device in Device Manager and scan for hardware changes
steps: Open Device Manager from the Start menu.
Expand Sound, video and game controllers.
If your audio device is listed, right-click it and select Enable device if that option appears.
If it is not listed, open the View menu and select Show hidden devices.
Open the Action menu and select Scan for hardware changes.

sources.signal: Official Microsoft page: Enable device, Show hidden devices, Scan for hardware changes
Microsoft Tech Community thread; user reports Scan for hardware changes re-added the missing monitor output (may not persist after sleep)

title: An app keeps using the wrong output device
symptoms: One app (for example a browser or music player) plays through a different device than the rest of Windows
An app does not follow when I change the output device from the taskbar
System sounds work but one app plays on the wrong device or not at all
causes: The app has its own output device set in Volume mixer (App volume and device preferences) instead of Default
Windows saved an old per-app device assignment that no longer matches the device you use

signals: A per-app audio routing preference points the app to a specific endpoint rather than the system default
An app's audio session is on a different render endpoint than the system default

fixes.title: Set the app's output device back to Default in Volume mixer
steps: Start playing sound in the affected app so it appears in the list.
On Windows 11, open Start > Settings > System > Sound > Volume mixer. On Windows 10, open Start > Settings > System > Sound > Advanced sound options (App volume and device preferences).
Find the app under Apps and set its Output device to Default, or to the device you want.
Make sure the app is not muted and its volume slider is raised.
Close the app fully and open it again.

sources.signal: Official Microsoft page 'Fix app audio not working while system sounds work in Windows': confirm the correct Output device for the app in Volume mixer
Microsoft Q&A moderator answer; OP confirms setting Edge back to Default in App volume and device preferences restores playback (can recur after the next device change)

fixes.title: Reset sound devices and volumes for all apps
steps: On Windows 11, open Start > Settings > System > Sound > Volume mixer. On Windows 10, open Start > Settings > System > Sound > Advanced sound options.
Next to Reset sound devices and volumes for all apps to the recommended defaults, select Reset.
Choose your output device again and set any app volumes you had customized.
